_about: Measured style targets (statistics only) from public-domain works in The Met's and the Cleveland Museum of Art's Open Access collections; see tools/measure_targets.py and docs/MANUAL.md, 'Report'.

renaissance._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
renaissance._rule: European Paintings 1400-1560 by Italian, Netherlandish, Flemish or German artists

baroque._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
baroque._rule: European Paintings 1600-1700 by Italian, Spanish, Flemish or French artists

dutch-golden-age._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works

romanticism._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
romanticism._rule: European and American paintings 1790-1850 by British, German, French or American artists

realism._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
realism._rule: European Paintings 1840-1880 by French artists (Realism and the Barbizon generation)

impressionism._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
impressionism._rule: European Paintings 1865-1895 by French artists, oil

post-impressionism._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
post-impressionism._rule: European Paintings 1885-1905 by French or Dutch artists

ukiyo-e._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works

east-asian-ink._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
east-asian-ink._rule: Asian Art: Chinese and Japanese paintings in ink, 1300-1900

byzantine-icon._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works; Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0 works)
byzantine-icon._rule: Paintings (Met: any department; Cleveland: type Painting) in tempera (egg tempera, tempera and gold) on wood, panel or linen, begun 1100-1850, whose culture or artist nationality is Byzantine, Greek/Cretan, Russian or Balkan Orthodox (Byzant-, Greek, Greece, Cret-, Russia-, Balkan, Bulgaria, Serbia, Romania, Macedonia, Cyprus, Novgorod, Moscow, Pskov, Yaroslavl); oil paintings (e.g. El Greco's Spanish work), mosaics, metalwork, textiles and manuscripts on parchment excluded

_works.medium: Tempera and gold on wood panel (poplar)

expressionism._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works; Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access (CC0 works)
expressionism._rule: Paintings, drawings and prints in colour (oil, tempera, watercolour, gouache, pastel, coloured chalk or crayon, colour prints) begun 1905-1925 by artists whose first-named nationality is German or Austrian (Met and Cleveland; postcards and other sheets under 16 cm, Met prints without a catalogued size, ornament and design drawings excluded, which removes the Wiener Werkstaette postcards); black-and-white prints and drawings (black chalk, crayon, charcoal, woodcut) are excluded because they would set the colour measures, not the current

pen-and-ink-illustration._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
pen-and-ink-illustration._rule: Drawings in pen and ink without wash, colour, chalk or charcoal, 1875-1920 (any department but Modern and Contemporary Art; trade designs titled 'Design for' or numbered '#' excluded): the illustrators' originals

etching-engraving._source: The Met Open Access (CC0), public-domain works
etching-engraving._rule: Drawings and Prints: intaglio prints whose medium begins 'Engraving' (1480-1900) or 'Etching' (1500-1925), black and white (no wood engraving, stipple, mezzotint, aquatint, crayon manner, roulette, soft-ground, colour or hand colouring)

graphite-hyperrealism._source: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs, FSA/OWI Black-and-White Negatives (no known restrictions on publication); random items, film rebate cropped (6% each side), converted to grey
graphite-hyperrealism._rule: the kind of photograph a graphite hyperrealist copies: monochrome photographs with optical focus, depth of field and a full value range. Proxy, not the style: hyperrealist drawings are in copyright. Near-black frames (p95 < L* 40) excluded. Colour measures omitted (monochrome)
graphite-hyperrealism._tool: studio/v8/eyes.py measure() via the same method as tools/measure_targets.py

_finished_drawings._source: The Met Open Access (CC0): finished 19th-century graphite portrait drawings, the most worked square window (the head) of each

graphite-hyperrealism-closeup._about: Close-up ruler for graphite-hyperrealism: fine measures (eyes.measure_fine) of openly licensed close-up photographs at their own resolution, in subject-mm (face, skin, hair) and at the sheet's 5 px/mm (whole frame). PROVISIONAL until at least 10 photographs. Subject keys (face, skin, hair) are bounded by the photographs' p10-p90 once there are 5; whole-frame keys by BOUND_RULES (judgements from docs/research/hyperrealism-gaps.md) on the mean. Every key keeps mean, sd, range and p10/p90: the spread across the photographs.
